title: The Songbook of Bellbird Bay
premise: Tamsin Delacroix built her career planning other people's perfect days while quietly nursing a decade-old wound: the night she and rival planner Jonah Reyes were stranded together in a snowstorm, confessed everything, and then pretended it never happened. When the eccentric matriarch of Bellbird Bay dies and leaves her crumbling seaside inn to whoever can prove they 'belong' to it, Tamsin and Jonah are forced to co-plan one last wedding there—and to confront what their silence cost them. As legal challenges from the town council mount and the deadline for claiming the inheritance looms, they discover the will's true test was never paperwork but the sentence each has rehearsed for ten years. In the end, they say it aloud at the inn's restored hearth, claim the inn together, and finally plan a wedding that is their own.
about_author: Rafael Ishikawa is a former event coordinator who spent six years orchestrating weddings along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction full-time. They write love stories about people who are excellent at caring for others and terrible at admitting what they want.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She runs a flawless wedding in San Francisco while privately cataloguing all the reasons she no longer believes in them, treating her heart like a muscle she has trained into obedience. A letter arrives: an inheritance in Bellbird Bay, contingent on conditions she doesn't yet understand. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Terms of Belonging
chapters.summary: Tamsin travels to Bellbird Bay and meets the late Edith Marsh's lawyer, who explains the will: the inn goes to two named heirs—Tamsin and a partner she must co-claim it with within ninety days. She learns the co-heir's name and goes cold. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Rival at the Gate
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah arrives expecting sole stewardship of the inn where he spent his boyhood summers, only to find Tamsin Delacroix on the porch. Their old rivalry reignites instantly, sharp and familiar. Emotional beat: anger as armor over something tender neither will name.

chapters.title: Edith's Conditions
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. The will requires them to jointly restore the inn and host one wedding there before the deadline—or the property passes to the town council, who want it demolished for a parking lot. They sign a grudging partnership agreement. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Inventory of Damage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Surveying the inn's decayed ballroom, she finds Edith's old songbook—handwritten setlists from decades of weddings—and a note addressed to 'the two who ran.' The first hint that Edith knew more than she let on. Emotional beat: haunted curiosity.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, flashback-heavy. The original snowstorm: two young planners stranded at this very inn, too much wine, a confession half-spoken, and Jonah walking out at dawn without saying goodbye. He understands now why Edith chose them both. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants Too Much
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A couple books the restoration wedding: Priya and Dev, whose families oppose the match and who want the ceremony to double as a public declaration. Tamsin recognizes her own avoidance mirrored in their courage. Emotional beat: uncomfortable self-recognition.

chapters.title: Council of Small Minds
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The town council, led by Councilman Harrow, contests the will, arguing neither heir has genuine ties to Bellbird Bay. Jonah digs up evidence of Edith's history with both their families. Emotional beat: first taste of fighting for something instead of against someone.

chapters.title: Sanding Down the Years
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Working side by side restoring the ballroom floor, the hostility thins into banter, then into the easy rhythm they had before the betrayal. A near-touch over a shared plank. Emotional beat: warmth arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: What the Songbook Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Deciphering Edith's songbook annotations, he realizes the setlists trace her own lost love—a woman she never married because the town wouldn't allow it. Justice outside the law has a lineage here. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Rain Check on Ruin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A storm knocks out power; by candlelight, Tamsin and Jonah almost repeat the past—but this time she stops him, demanding words before anything else. He deflects. Emotional beat: hope wounded by old cowardice.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Harrow privately offers Jonah sole ownership if he'll testify Tamsin is a stranger to the bay—an offer calibrated to their rivalry. Jonah refuses, but says nothing to Tamsin, and the secret starts to fester. Emotional beat: loyalty tested in private.

chapters.title: Priya and Dev's Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The couple's rehearsal dinner becomes a small battlefield when disapproving family members arrive uninvited; Tamsin defends them fiercely, discovering she believes in weddings again—for other people. Emotional beat: conviction rekindled at second hand.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Harrow leaks word of his offer to the local paper, framing Jonah as a schemer. Tamsin reads it before he can explain, and the decade-old pattern repeats: silence mistaken for betrayal. Emotional beat: the wound reopened exactly where it always breaks.

chapters.title: Separate Rooms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They work in shifts, communicating through notes on the songbook pages. One note—hers, unfinished, 'the thing I should have said in the snow was'—is found and read by Jonah, who cannot bring himself to answer. Emotional beat: longing conducted through paper.

chapters.title: Edith's Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the attic he finds Edith's unsent letters to her lost love, including one that names the sentence she rehearsed for forty years. He copies it out, understanding that the will's real condition was always this: say it before time runs out. Emotional beat: revelation as instruction.

chapters.title: Ninety Days Become Nine
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Legal filings accelerate; the hearing is moved up to the day after the wedding. With the inn still half-restored and the co-heirs barely speaking, Tamsin makes a decision: finish the work, win or lose, together or not. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Wedding at Bellbird Bay
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Priya and Dev marry in the restored ballroom as the whole town watches—including Harrow, visibly moved despite himself. During the vows, Tamsin and Jonah stand on opposite sides of the room, each mouthing along to words meant for someone else. Emotional beat: joy sharpening private ache.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Before the council, Jonah publicly recounts the snowstorm, the betrayal, and Harrow's bribe, submitting Edith's letters as proof that belonging is proven by staying, not by paperwork. The town turns. Emotional beat: justice won at the cost of total exposure.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the inn's relit hearth, with the deed settled and the town gone home, Tamsin finally says the sentence she rehearsed for a decade: that she loved him in the snow, loves him now, and is done training her heart to be quiet. Jonah answers with his own version. Emotional beat: catharsis—the withheld thing finally spoken.

chapters.title: Setlist for Two
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They add a new page to Edith's songbook together, choosing the music for a wedding of their own—small, imperfect, theirs. The inn's future is planned in margins and pencil. Emotional beat: tenderness after long drought.

chapters.title: Bellbird Bay, Open
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. One year later: the inn hosts its first season of weddings run by two partners whose names share the deed and, soon, a surname. Tamsin teaches a young planner that hearts aren't muscles to contain but instruments to learn. Final emotional beat: belonging, claimed at last.
